title: Daily Market Digest
subtitle: Markets Closed - Summary for Friday, October 23, 2026

items.headline: AI Concerns and Rising Oil Prices Drive Markets Lower on Friday
items.summary: U.S. equity markets closed predominantly lower on Friday, October 23, 2026, as investor sentiment was dampened by persistent concerns over the sustainability of artificial intelligence (AI) investments and a significant surge in crude oil prices. The selling pressure extended beyond the tech sector, though some chip stocks did see a rebound. Not financial advice.

items.headline: Ai Okto Corp. soared on Friday.
items.summary: Ai Okto Corp. ($AIOK) was a notable gainer, surging 182.8% to $12.02.

items.headline: Cybersecurity stocks like CrowdStrike rallied.
items.summary: CrowdStrike ($CRWD) rose 8.25% to $257.57, amid increased demand for protection following critical PHP security vulnerabilities.

items.headline: Crown Castle gained on SpaceX lease talks.
items.summary: Crown Castle ($CCI) climbed 9.10% following reports that SpaceX is in talks to lease space on its cell towers, potentially a multi-billion dollar deal.

items.headline: Davion Healthcare PLC plummeted.
items.summary: Davion Healthcare PLC ($DAVI) was among the biggest decliners, dropping 48.5% to $6.00.

items.headline: AT&T fell on Starlink competition fears.
items.summary: AT&T ($T) dropped 7.96% amid concerns about competition from SpaceX's Starlink, which is reportedly eying 80,000 cell sites across the US.

items.headline: Flagstar Bank declined after revenue miss.
items.summary: Flagstar Bank ($FLG) shed 9.27% following a revenue miss in its latest earnings report.

items.headline: Energy Leads as Defensive Sectors Lag Amid Market Shift
items.summary: Energy was the top-performing sector, rising 2.60% due to surging crude oil prices. Technology also saw gains (+0.49%) as some chip stocks rebounded. Conversely, defensive sectors like Consumer Staples (-1.92%), Communication Services (-1.78%), and Health Care (-1.11%) underperformed, suggesting a shift in market leadership on a day where most sectors finished lower.

items.headline: Initial Jobless Claims Fall, Consumer Sentiment Dips
items.summary: Initial jobless claims decreased by 6,000 to 194,000 for the week ended October 17. Meanwhile, the Conference Board reported that the leading indicator for September remained unchanged. U.S. consumer sentiment edged down to near a record low in October, reflecting concerns over rising prices. The 10-year Treasury yield rose to 4.99%.

items.headline: Meta Posts Strong Earnings, but AI Spending Remains a Concern
items.summary: Meta Platforms Inc. ($META) reported robust third-quarter 2026 earnings, with revenues up 26% year-over-year to $64.6 billion and adjusted earnings per share of $7.40. However, despite strong results, market participants expressed deep concerns about the sustainability of massive spending on AI data centers and future capital expenditure guidance from major tech players, contributing to the broader market's cautious sentiment.

items.headline: Oil Prices Surge on Geopolitical Tensions; AI Spending Under Scrutiny
items.summary: Brent crude oil prices climbed 3.1% to over $116 a barrel, reaching their highest level since June 2022, fueled by fresh Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and escalating Middle East tensions. This surge amplified inflation worries. Simultaneously, the sustainability of huge AI data center investments continued to weigh on investor minds, with some proposals emerging from the Senate to address worker displacement due to AI.
